{{Quote|The platoon sergeant had previously distinguished his unit in operations on Balmorra, Lasan, and the Metellos Ring.|[[TX-5532]], ''Imperial Handbook: A Commander's Guide''|<ref name="ImperialHandbook">''[[Star Wars: Imperial Handbook: A Commander's Guide]]''</ref>}}
'''Lasan''' was a [[Wild Space/Legends|Wild Space]] [[Planet/Legends|planet]]. An arid and [[Temperature/Legends|warm]] world, its surface featured [[Desert/Legends|desert]] and plains as well as high [[Mountain/Legends|mountains]]. Lasan was [[Homeworld/Legends|inhabited]] by [[Diet/Legends|herbivorous]] [[Bantha/Legends|banthas]] and the [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]], [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoid]] [[Lasat/Legends|Lasat]].

The Lasat were mostly nomadic, tribe-based [[Trapper/Legends|trappers]] at a relatively low level of technology; however, a few regions on Lasan had developed [[City/Legends|city]]-states with social stratification and feudal-level technology, including comparatively advanced applied [[Chemist/Legends|chemistry]]. Lasan was an isolated world that was seldom visited by interstellar [[Merchant/Legends|traders]], and only a handful of the Lasat were found in the wider [[The galaxy/Legends|galaxy]]. By [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]], the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] waged the conflicts known as the [[Lasan Suppression]] and the [[Siege of Lasan/Legends|Siege of Lasan]].

==Description==
Lasan was an isolated terrestrial [[Planet/Legends|planet]]<ref name="AlienEncounters" /> located in the [[Lasan system]], a part of [[Wild Space/Legends|Wild Space]].<ref name="EAOC" /> The planet's surface featured expansive [[Desert/Legends|desert]] and plains that were divided by high [[Mountain/Legends|mountains]]. Lasan's climate was arid and [[Temperature/Legends|warm]], although the [[Standard day/Legends|nights]] in the desert were cold. The [[Species/Legends|fauna]] of Lasan included [[Bantha/Legends|banthas]], [[Diet/Legends|herbivorous]] herd animals that migrated between seasonal grazing grounds,<ref name="AlienEncounters" /> and other, larger herbivores.<ref name="Journal11" />

==History==
{{Quote|Tango Company fought during the Lasan Suppression, earning its members the Imperial Medal of Valor.|[[TX-5532]], ''Imperial Handbook: A Commander's Guide''|<ref name="ImperialHandbook" />}}
A complete survey of Lasan had never been performed, with the initial survey revealing the planet's terrain features. Evidence suggested that the first [[Lasat/Legends|Lasat]], members of Lasan's [[Homeworld/Legends|native]] [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] species, who traveled offworld did so after being [[Slavery/Legends|captured]] by [[Slaver/Legends|slavers]]. However, those Lasat were soon released, as they made poor slaves and were potentially dangerous because of their typically advanced [[Chemist/Legends|chemistry]] skills. Overall, only a handful of Lasat were found in the wider [[The galaxy/Legends|galaxy]].<ref name="Journal11" />

During the [[Imperial Era/Legends|reign]] of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], [[Tango Company/Legends|Tango Company]] of the Imperial [[Stormtrooper Corps/Legends|Stormtrooper Corps]] fought during the conflict known as the [[Lasan Suppression]]. The [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtroopers]] of the [[501st Legion/Legends|501st Legion's]] [[Negastrike platoon]] also participated in an operation on Lasan. Subsequently, Tango Company's and Negastrike [[Platoon/Legends|platoon's]] operations on Lasan were mentioned in the ''[[Imperial Handbook: A Commander's Guide]]'', an [[Imperial Military/Legends|Imperial Military]] manual published<ref name="ImperialHandbook" /> by [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]].<ref name="Date">''[[Star Wars: Imperial Handbook: A Commander's Guide]]'' is presented as an [[Imperial Handbook: A Commander's Guide|in-universe document]] published during the life of [[Wilhuff Tarkin/Legends|Wilhuff Tarkin]], who [[Death/Legends|perished]] in [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]] per ''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''.</ref> At some point by that same [[Standard year/Legends|year]],<ref name="SiegeDate">''[[Forged in Battle]]'' establishes that the [[Siege of Lasan/Legends|Siege of Lasan]] took place during the existence of the [[Imperial Senate/Legends|Imperial Senate]], which was [[Dissolution of the Imperial Senate/Legends|dissolved]] in [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]] per ''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''.</ref> the Empire also waged the conflict known as the [[Siege of Lasan/Legends|Siege of Lasan]], in which [[Imperial Security Bureau/Legends|Imperial Security Bureau]] agents [[Death/Legends|slaughtered]] numerous Lasat civilians as a show of Imperial might.<ref name="Forged">''[[Forged in Battle]]''</ref>

When the [[Merchant/Legends|trader]] [[To'iir]] consulted the [[Trader's Gamble]] feature of the [[Lantillian Spacers' Brotherhood/Legends|Lantillian Spacers' Brotherhood's]] [[Free-Trader's Guide]] service for a possible hiding place from Imperial [[Moff/Legends|Moff]] [[Roff]]'s forces, the service erroneously listed Lasan, named "Lasat," as being located in [[The Slice/Legends|the Slice]] portion of the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]]. After going through a list of fourteen planets, including "Lasat," To'iir decided he and his partner, [[Liadden]], would travel to [[Gamorr/Legends|Gamorr]]<ref name="Journal10">{{JournalCite|10|A Free-Trader's Guide to the Planets}}</ref> in the Outer Rim.<ref name="TEA">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref>

==Inhabitants==
{{Main|Lasat/Legends}}
[[File:Lasat-AE.png|thumb|right|125px|The Lasat were native to Lasan.]]
Lasan was inhabited by the Lasat,<ref name="AlienEncounters" /> a species of sentient, [[Rodent/Legends|rodent]]-like,<ref name="Encyclopedia">''[[Star Wars Encyclopedia]]''</ref> carnivorous<ref name="AlienEncounters" /> [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoids]] descended from a [[Dog/Legends|canine]] species.<ref name="CSWE">{{CSWECite|II|246|Lasat}}</ref> The Lasat used a [[Language/Legends|spoken]] [[Lasat language/Legends|language]] to pass down their history via a rich mythological tradition despite also having developed a simple hieroglyphic script.<ref name="AlienEncounters" />

The Lasat were mostly tribal-based nomads, with more primitive, stone age-level tribes using simple [[Trapper/Legends|traps]] to catch minor animals for [[Foodstuff/Legends|food]], and [[Net/Legends|nets]] and [[Spear/Legends|spears]] for larger game. The more technologically advanced Lasat tribes followed bantha herds and trapped them to obtain [[Hair/Legends|wool]], meat, and [[Leather/Legends|hides]].<ref name="AlienEncounters" />

Some groups of Lasat, considered to be more civilized, were at an early feudal level of technology and were developing rudimentary [[Metallurgy/Legends|metal-working]]. Socially-stratified Lasat [[City/Legends|city]]-states had also been developed in a few regions of the planet, and the urban-dwelling Lasat were practicing applied chemistry at disproportionately advanced levels. Few interstellar merchants made deals with the Lasat. The occasional [[free-trader]]s that visited Lasan only exported the local [[Carpet/Legends|rugs]] and [[Tapestry/Legends|tapestries]].<ref name="AlienEncounters" />

Both the tribal and urban Lasat were governed by [[Theocracy|religious monarchs]], and small-scale conflicts between neighboring Lasat communities were fought by a [[Soldier/Legends|warrior]]-[[Law enforcement agency/Legends|police]] caste. In those wars, the city-states increasingly employed the tribes of nomadic Lasat as [[Mercenary/Legends|mercenaries]].<ref name="AlienEncounters" />

Although the Lasat society was largely nomadic, two regions on Lasan had developed city-states. The Lasat inhabiting cities lived in buildings made out of mud bricks.<ref name="AlienEncounters" /> The Lantillian Spacers' Brotherhood's Free-Trader's Guide service categorized the planet "Lasat" as having a "[[Spaceport/Legends|Starport]] of Limited Services or less."<ref name="Journal10" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|Although the Brotherhood has verified facts where possible, no guarantee of accuracy is assured or implied.|The Free-Trader's Guide service warning in "A Free-Trader's Guide to the Planets"|<ref name="Journal10" />}}
[[File:SWAJ10.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Lasan was introduced as "Lasat" in ''Star Wars Adventure Journal'' 10.]]
The planet named "Lasat" was introduced in "[[A Free-Trader's Guide to the Planets]]," an article written by [[Timothy S. O'Brien|Timothy O'Brien]] and published in [[May]] [[1996]] in the [[West End Games]]' [[Star Wars Adventure Journal 10|''Star Wars Adventure Journal'' 10]].<ref name="Journal10" /> In the "[[Alien Encounters (article series)|Alien Encounters]]" feature of the [[November]] 1996 [[Star Wars Adventure Journal 11|''Star Wars Adventure Journal'' 11]], O'Brien instead used "Lasat" as the name for a species native to the world of "Lasan,"<ref name="Journal11" /> a spelling repeated in all further sources mentioning the planet.<ref name="AlienEncounters" /><ref name="ImperialHandbook" /><ref name="CSWE" />

In "A Free-Trader's Guide to the Planets," "Lasat" is listed among the names of fourteen planets provided [[in-universe]] by the Lantillian Spacers' Brotherhood's Free-Trader's Guide service as potential destinations for free-traders in the Slice portion of the Outer Rim Territories. The list, which the service erroneously claims contains thirteen entries, also names three planets&mdash;[[Kirdo III/Legends|Kirdo III]], "Lasat," and "[[Ossel II|Ossell II]]"<ref name="Journal10" /> (a misspelling of the planet Ossel II)<ref name="GG4">[[Galaxy Guide 4: Alien Races (Second Edition)|''Galaxy Guide 4: Alien Races'', Second Edition]]</ref>&mdash;whose respective [[Star system/Legends|star systems]] the [[2009]] reference book ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'' placed in regions other than the Slice, with the Lasan system being placed in grid square P-20, Rimward of the [[Trailing Sectors/Legends|Trailing Sectors]].<ref name="TEA" />

Given the aforementioned information, as well as the fact that the Free-Trader's Guide issues an in-universe warning about the potential inaccuracy of the information it provides, this article assumes the inconsistencies regarding information on Lasan between "A Free-Trader's Guide to the Planets" and other sources arise due to erroneous in-universe information presented by the Free-Trader's Guide.<ref name="Journal10" />
